what_it_does: Modern processors execute multiple instructions per cycle to improve performance, but this typically requires complex out-of-order logic that burns significant power. In-order processors are simpler and more energy-efficient but only execute one instruction per cycle, leaving performance on the table. This paper focuses on mixed workloads where some instructions operate on integers and others on floating-point numbers. The key insight is that integer and floating-point instructions often don't depend on each other, so they can be executed in parallel, allowing a simple in-order design to execute two instructions per cycle when the types alternate.
